correctness.rationale: For every connected graph the Laplacian columns affinely span the zero-sum hyperplane, and their barycentric facet normals are exactly the nonzero pseudoinverse columns. Equalizing each normalized facet clearance yields the unique incenter, while their sum proves the global inradius optimum. For trees, Cauchy--Schwarz, the positive Laplacian spectrum, the resistance/Wiener identity and a self-contained leaf-deletion Wiener upper bound prove the universal n^-5/2 lower bound. The degree-sum estimate gives at least (n+2)/2 vertices of degree ≤2; each possesses a large neighboring branch whose cut current enforces a pseudoinverse-column norm ≥(n-1)/(2 sqrt(2)n), giving the universal n^-1 upper bound. Explicit zero-sum solutions to the Laplacian column equations produce the star and path formulas, with a positive Riemann-integrable limiting quartic proving their distinct exact asymptotic constants. All dimensions n≥2 and normalizations have been reconstructed; finite exact arithmetic is corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The full primary 2017 arXiv paper defining Laplacian simplices was inspected at the defining graph-Laplacian construction, its general facets and operations, and Section 4 including Proposition 4.1. Its central equivalence theorem treats lattice geometry, not intrinsic Euclidean inspheres; full-document searches found no inradius or circumradius result. The same-object sequel and the nearby effective-resistance simplex literature were also inspected at their definitions and relevant results. A symmetry-restricted spectral identity for vertex-transitive graph Laplacian simplices cannot cover nonregular trees (except the two-vertex tree), and the more general barycentric formula by itself does not entail the new universal tree bounds or differing path/star asymptotic powers. Candidate-specific published-literature and mathematical-record searches covered the canonical column simplex, pseudoinverse normals, lattice equivalence, tree paths and stars, Wiener index, and sharp exponents. No result implying the all-tree radius window and sharp two-exponent separation was found.

value.rationale: The Braun--Meyer all-tree unimodular-equivalence theorem makes tree Laplacian simplices the canonical test of which geometric properties survive lattice equivalence. The proved result uncovers a polynomially diverging Euclidean shape difference invisible to every unimodular invariant: paths have inradius of order n^-5/2 while stars have order n^-1, and the all-tree bound shows these powers delimit the entire possible scale window. The sharp-exponent classification is structurally motivated by different graph topologies and is supported by exact star and quartic path norm laws, not merely by generic simplex normalization or a small numerical improvement. It connects lattice polytope geometry, tree electrical flows and Wiener index inequalities and gives a natural starting point for finer tree extremal problems.
